verdict.rationale: Kong's GitHub README documents running Kong Gateway yourself: a Docker install in DB-less mode, a local Admin API (:8001) and Kong Manager UI (:8002), native Kubernetes via the official Ingress Controller, and declarative or hybrid deployment "without any vendor lock-in". An official `kong-gateway` Terraform provider is "designed for use with Kong Gateway on-prem", which further confirms the self-hosted deployment target. Missing for 10: an explicit open-source license statement in the evidence, independent hands-on corroboration of a fully self-hosted setup, and clarity that the docs quickstart puts the control plane in Konnect SaaS rather than fully self-hosted.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: there is also a docker installation procedure if you’d prefer to run the Kong Gateway in DB-less mode.
Sophisticated deployment models like Declarative Databaseless Deployment and Hybrid Deployment (control plane/data plane separation) without any vendor lock-in.
Kong runs natively on Kubernetes thanks to its official Kubernetes Ingress Controller.
:8002 - access Kong's management Web UI ([Kong Manager](https://github.com/Kong/kong-manager)) on [localhost:8002](http://localhost:8002)
Designed for use with Kong Gateway on-prem, the `kong-gateway` provider allows you to manage Kong Entities using Terraform
